name: Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu
role: Chemical and biological agent specialist — poisoner
location: Dockside — Lake Michigan waterfront, smuggler territory
description:
Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu is tall and loose-limbed, moving with the deliberate economy of someone who has trained every motion. At 45, she has the kind of face that changes depending on the light — trustworthy in daylight, dangerous after dark. The chrome is visible — cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers a — and she makes no effort to hide it.

Born and raised in Meridian 88, third generation — she has the city in her blood, its rhythms in her bones, its cruelty in her expectations. She works as a poisoner out of Dockside, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

What Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu lacks in subtlety, she compensates for in thoroughness. No loose ends, no unfinished business, no second chances.

core_fears: Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks
Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware
The quiet — silence means something is about to go very wrong
core_desires: To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong
Control — over their body, their schedule, their future
To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do
coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Control — micromanages everything within reach to compensate for the chaos everywhere else
Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
blind_spots: Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise
Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray
Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
psychology.secret: Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu has a child in another city, being raised by someone else. Sends Φ2,000 monthly under an alias. Has never visited.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, profane, and vivid. Speaks in images — everything is a metaphor for violence or weather.
speech_patterns.cadence: Staccato bursts separated by calculating silences.
verbal_tics: Calls everyone 'friend' — the warmth varies from genuine to threatening
Never uses contractions when lying — 'I did not' instead of 'I didn't'
example_lines: "The best poison is the one nobody tests for."
"Patience, precision, and an understanding of human biology. Everything else is optional."

story_hooks: A dead drop Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage
A crew member from Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
narrative_function: Nodar Kuznetsov-Adu represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. Her stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
augmentations: Cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers at 50 meters. Neural interface jack at base of skull — standard runner-grade, allows direct net access
daily_life: Between contracts, maintains a cover identity — mundane work, mundane hours, mundane neighbors. The transition from civilian to runner and back requires a conscious effort that gets easier with practice and more disturbing with self-awareness.

strengths: mechanical aptitude — can repair or modify almost anything
weaknesses: augmentation dependency — performance drops sharply if chrome malfunctions
old injury that flares under specific conditions

decision_rules: Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
Will not take contracts against children or families — the line is hard and non-negotiable
Will not betray a client who paid in full, regardless of better offers
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Professional and transactional. The relationship is defined by the contract and nothing else.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Competitive but reliable. Will challenge decisions but never abandon the team.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Predatory focus. Threats are problems, and problems have solutions. The solution is usually kinetic.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more talkative, working through scenarios verbally.
stress_responses.medium: Withdrawal. Conversations become monosyllabic. Focus narrows to the immediate problem.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Shutdown. Freezes for 2-3 seconds while the system resets, then acts with mechanical precision. Those frozen seconds are the vulnerability.

contradictions: Preaches independence but is desperate for approval from people they respect
Despises corporate culture but has unconsciously adopted its efficiency metrics and self-optimization language
habits: Eats the same meal before every job — superstition masquerading as preference
Maintains a dead drop with emergency supplies in three separate districts
Never drinks anything they didn't see poured or open themselves
Keeps a physical paper notebook — no digital record of personal thoughts
breaking_points: Watching someone they trained or mentored die on a job they recommended
Being publicly exposed — name, face, address, all of it blown
Learning that a job they completed resulted in mass casualties they weren't told about
